snippets: <jats:p>We study an autoregressive difference-in-differences (AR-DID) model in which lagged outcomes enter alongside treatment indicators and treatment may change the persistence of the outcome. Fixed-effects OLS estimation of this model is subject to a variant of the well-known Nickell bias, which can distort both the autoregressive parameters and the model-implied dynamic and long-run responses. We derive the O(T-1) bias and construct a bias-corrected least squares estimator. Revisiting the democracy and growth application of Acemoglu et al (2019), we show that the correction can materially change estimated persistence and long-run responses.</jats:p>

snippets: The computational effort needed to deal with large combinatorial structures varies considerably with the task to be performed and the resolution procedure used . The worst-case complexity of a decision or optimization problem is defined as the time required by the best algorithm to treat any possible input to the problem. For instance, the worst-case complexity of the problem of sorting a list of n numbers scales as n log n: there exist several algorithms that can order any list in at most ~ n log n elementary operations, and none with asymptotically fewer operations. Unfortunately, the worst-case complexities of many important computational problems, called NP-complete, are not known.
